title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 24, 2026This Clásico could be season-defining. / Alex Caparros - UEFA/Getty Images (Barcelona), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Real Madrid)El Clásico is unlikely to ever fade from global relevance, but there’s no denying that one of Europe’s most illustrious fixtures has lost a bit of sparkle over the past decade.
This was once the pinnacle of the sport. The soccer world stopped when Barcelona and Real Madrid locked horns, and Pep Guardiola and José Mourinho paraded their respective dugouts.

Well, Mourinho is back, folks, and preparing himself for his first Clásico since 2013. His relationship with Barça dates back to his time as Sir Bobby Robson’s translator/assistant in the mid-90s, and the resentment that washed over him after the club he once adored opted to hire Guardiola as Frank Rijkaard’s assistant in 2008 has struggled to fade.

He was Barça’s arch-nemesis for a period, and he eventually broke Guardiola’s outstanding team, not to mention his Spanish counterpart on the touchline. However, Hansi Flick’s current Blaugrana are on track to smash the records set by Mourinho’s Madrid in 2011–12.

Sunday’s hosts head into the Clásico six points clear of the visitors and are threatening to run away with the division for a third successive year. Camp Nou was the site of Mourinho’s “most beautiful defeat,” but he can’t afford a loss of any kind this weekend. A nine-point deficit to this Barcelona team would feel unassailable, even at this early juncture and with the swathe of superstars Los Blancos possess.

The world’s best clash on Sunday. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesBarcelona have won six of the previous seven meetings against their Clásico rivals, including two of the three duels last season. Flick has generally had a hold over Real Madrid, but the return of Mourinho adds an extra layer of intrigue and potential scope for the unexpected.
Mourinho has locked horns with Flick just once in his managerial career, with his Tottenham Hotspur team losing 3–1 at Bayern Munich in 2019. Flick’s Bayern would go on to conquer all that season.

There‘s a sense that Madrid remain somewhat unsophisticated, certainly relative to Barça, but a Mourinho-led team in 2026 doesn’t require tactical perfection. It looks like the returning manager is going down the Carlo Ancelotti route, taking a more laissez-faire approach and ensuring his team has the right balance. They’ve been good over the past week, albeit against opponents incomparable to their upcoming test.
Barcelona are outstanding, but if Madrid click in Catalonia, we could be in for something special.

There were a couple of notable injury casualties at Parc des Princes on Tuesday evening. Most notably, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his ACL, but Barcelona were also struck by the bug. Dani Olmo sustained a groin injury that’ll keep him out for the next month.
The hosts at least have the opportunistic Fermín López to call upon in reserve.

Flick is also set to be without full backs Jules Koundé and Eric García, meaning João Cancelo and young Xavi Espart will likely retain their spots in defense. Espart was excellent in Paris, but Cancelo struggled.

Rodri played just 30 minutes in the week, with the Barcelona manager likely having an eye on this fixture. The Spaniard, preparing for his first taste of the Clásico, will start alongside Pedri in midfield.
Lamine Yamal and Raphinha are shoo-ins in attack, so Flick will have to decide between Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi down the left-hand side.
Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Real Madrid (4-2-3-1): J. García; Espart, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Gordon; Raphinha.

Real Madrid are functioning just fine without Vinícius Júnior, who’s serving the second of his four-match ban on Sunday. The Brazilian was punished for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in Madrid’s 1–0 victory over Villarreal earlier this month and subsequently remonstrating with the referee.

The in-form Yan Diomande will start down the left in his absence, and Mourinho is poised to deploy a French midfield tandem comprising Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga. Federico Valverde will be shunted out to right back, and Arda Güler will operate freely from the right-side of midfield.
The visitors are missing Ferland Mendy, Raúl Asencio and Rodrygo due to injury.
Real Madrid Predicted Lineup vs. Barcelona (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Valverde, Konaté, Huijsen, Cucurella; Tchouaméni, Camavinga; Güler, Bellingham, Diomande; Mbappé.
